gap: No result ChatGPT got works out how much RAM each NAS has left once Home Assistant's own 2 GB VM minimum is taken out. On a stock Synology DS225+ the answer is none: it ships with 2 GB, and Synology runs VMs only on units with more than 2 GB. The DS925+ keeps 2 GB for DSM, while the QNAP TS-264-8G and UGREEN DXP2800 each keep 6 GB.
standout_why: Synology's VMM spec page (cited by ChatGPT) gives the 'more than 2 GB' rule but no per-model RAM. home-assistant.io/installation/linux gives the 2 GB / 2 vCPU HAOS minimum but no NAS models. raspberry.tips (top result for UGREEN) gives the VM 4 GB of the DXP2800's 8 GB and measured 15–17 W idle, but it covers one model only and never subtracts anything for Synology or QNAP. QNAP's and UGREEN's passthrough FAQs have no RAM or power numbers. ChatGPT's answer says '8 GB minimum recommended' without linking it to any model's base RAM. Our current page notes the 'needs >2 GB' rule in the Synology cell, but it never does the subtraction or says a stock DS225+ cannot start a VM. I could not open the smarthomejunkie DXP4800 GT guide (certificate error).
decides: This takes the Synology DS225+ out of the 'buy and run' group: it needs a RAM module before VMM will start any VM. It also shows the DS925+ (4 GB ECC) leaves only 2 GB for DSM next to a 2 GB HAOS VM, so an upgrade is realistically required there too. The 8 GB QNAP TS-264 and UGREEN DXP2800 run HAOS out of the box with 6 GB to spare. So on headroom the pick goes to TS-264 or DXP2800; Zigbee passthrough reliability is still the separate deciding factor. The power figures add that any NAS host draws roughly 10× more always-on energy than a Home Assistant Green (about 140–255 kWh a year against 14.9 kWh). That matters only if the NAS would not otherwise be running 24/7.

findings.label: HAOS VM minimum resources
findings.value: 2 GB RAM, 2 vCPUs, UEFI boot required; 32 GB default disk (Unraid example)
findings.note: Used as the RAM subtracted for every NAS below.

findings.label: Synology VMM host RAM rule and USB passthrough
findings.value: VMs run only on Synology NAS with more than 2 GB memory; USB 2.0/3.0 passthrough supported (not on Virtual DSM)
findings.source_title: Virtual Machine Manager Technical Specifications | Synology Inc.
findings.note: Same page: VMM reserves at least one CPU thread for the host.

findings.label: RAM left after a 2 GB HAOS VM
findings.value: 0 GB at stock (VMM will not run); 4 GB after upgrading to the 6 GB maximum
findings.note: Ships 2 GB DDR4 non-ECC; VMM needs >2 GB, so no VM at stock. Upgraded: 6 GB − 2 GB = 4 GB. Power: 16.98 W access, 6.08 W HDD hibernation; 2× USB 3.2 Gen 1; 3-year warranty.

findings.label: RAM left after a 2 GB HAOS VM
findings.value: 2 GB at stock; 30 GB at the 32 GB maximum
findings.note: 4 GB DDR4 ECC − 2 GB = 2 GB; 32 GB − 2 GB = 30 GB. AMD Ryzen V1500B 4C/8T; 2× USB 3.2 Gen 1; 37.91 W access, 12.33 W HDD hibernation; 3-year warranty.

findings.label: RAM left after a 2 GB HAOS VM
findings.value: 6 GB at stock; 14 GB at the 16 GB maximum
findings.note: 8 GB − 2 GB = 6 GB; 16 GB − 2 GB = 14 GB. Celeron N5095 4C/4T; 2× USB 2.0 + 2× USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A; 18.288 W disk standby, 29.086 W typical (drives fully populated); 3-year warranty.

findings.label: RAM left after a 2 GB HAOS VM
findings.value: 6 GB at stock (4 GB in raspberry.tips' 4 GB-VM setup)
